tests.description: Verify orchestrate.rb, score_job_application.rb, and integrate_analysis.rb use .update() not .update_columns()

locations: Line 32: existing_ai_summary.update_columns(status: :extracting) — initial status set, broadcast not needed
Line 175: update_columns(status: :retrying, ...) — error handler rescue block
Line 180: update_columns(status: :failed, ...) — JSON parse error rescue block
Line 184: update_columns(status: :failed, ...) — general error rescue block
generate.rb.note: generate.rb was NOT one of the three specified files, but it uses update_columns in 4 places. The error-handler update_columns calls for :retrying and :failed bypass the broadcast_status_change callback. This means broadcast will NOT fire when generate.rb transitions to failed/retrying via its rescue blocks. Whether this is intentional (error statuses from generate shouldn't broadcast) or a bug depends on design intent.

tests.name: update_summary_status_record sets updated_at
tests.description: Transition a summary to succeeded, verify the status record's updated_at is set to approximately now and all denormalized columns are copied

details.note: update_summary_status_record uses update_columns with explicit updated_at: Time.current, so the timestamp is set correctly despite update_columns normally not touching timestamps

observations.description: generate.rb uses update_columns for error-state transitions (retrying, failed), which bypasses the broadcast_status_change callback. This means the frontend will NOT receive ActionCable broadcasts when generate.rb encounters errors. The three specified service files (orchestrate.rb, score_job_application.rb, integrate_analysis.rb) all use .update(), so their status transitions DO trigger broadcasts.

The update_summary_status_record method also uses update_columns (in the model itself, line 68), but explicitly includes updated_at: Time.current. This is correct — update_columns skips callbacks and timestamp auto-updates, but the explicit Time.current value ensures updated_at is set.
The broadcast_status_change callback uses a rescue StandardError => e block that logs and swallows errors, preventing ActionCable failures from aborting the status update. This is a safe pattern.
